title: Protocol for in vitro lysine deacetylation to test putative substrates of class III deacetylases
protocol: Transfect cells in the hood.
Mix 10 μg of substrate DNA with 250 μL Opti-MEM.
Gently invert 18 μL Lipofectamine 2000 mixed with 250 μL Opti-MEM.
Let both mixtures stand for 5 min, then combine them in one tube.
Incubate the combined mixture at room temperature (23°C) for 20 min.
Add the mixture drop-wise to 5–6 million HEK 293T cells in a 60 mm dish.
Gently mix the cells.
Mix 5 μg of deacetylase DNA with 250 μL Opti-MEM.
Gently invert 10 μL Lipofectamine 2000 mixed with 250 μL Opti-MEM.
Let both mixtures stand for 5 min, then combine them in one tube.
Incubate the combined mixture at room temperature (23°C) for 20 min.
Add the mixture drop-wise to 5–6 million HEK 293T cells in a 60 mm dish.
Gently mix the cells.
Incubate the cells with transfection reagents and DNA for about 16 hours overnight.
Incubate HEK 293T cells at 37°C with 5% CO2 content.
Check the cell confluency and viability of the transfected cells from day 1.
Trypsinize the cells and split each dish equally into two 10 cm dishes for a total of four 10 cm dishes.
Add Tricostatin A (TSA) to a final concentration of 0.5 μM to the cells with substrate transfection only.
Add nicotinamide to a final concentration of 1 μM to inhibit class I and II, and class III acetyltransferases respectively.
Let the cells incubate overnight for 12–16 hours to maximize acetylation.
Trypsinize the cells and collect them in an Eppendorf tube by combining duplicate dishes into one tube.
Add an equal amount of media to neutralize the trypsin.
Centrifuge the cells at 3,500 × g – 5,000 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant carefully without disturbing the cell pellet.
Wash the cells once with 1 mL of PBS and spin again at 3,500 × g – 5,000 × g for 5 min.
Remove the supernatant after washing, leaving only the cell pellet behind.
Lysate each tube of cells using about 400 μL–500 μL of cell lysis buffer.
Gently rotate or place the tubes on a rocker at 4°C for 30–40 min.
Spin the lysed cells down at maximum speed (∼17,000 × g) for 15 min at 4°C.
Prepare beads for pre-clearing the lysate by using 30 μL of a slurry of 50% beads per 500 μL of lysate.
Spin the beads down and wash them twice with 500 μL lysis buffer.
Resuspend the washed beads in lysis buffer to half the initial volume of the bead slurry.
Spin the beads for 30 seconds at 100 × g.
Turn the tubes 180 degrees and spin again for 30 seconds at 100 × g.
Remove supernatant, leaving only the beads behind.
Add 500 μL lysis buffer to the beads.
Repeat the spinning process as described previously.
Remove the buffer, leaving only the beads behind.
Keep the beads on ice and centrifuge at 4°C.
Use CL-4B Sepharose beads for pre-clearing FLAG-tagged substrates.
For mouse IP antibodies, use protein G agarose beads for preclearing.
For rabbit IP antibodies, use protein A agarose beads for preclearing.
Transfer the supernatant to a clean tube after the spin is complete from step 13; discard cell debris.
Add 30 μL of pre-clearing beads per every 500 μL of lysate.
Rotate the mixture at 4°C for 15 minutes.
Prepare conjugated beads as described in step 12, using 30 μL of a 50% slurry per every 500 μL of lysate.
Spin the lysate and beads down using conditions used in step 12 for washing the beads.
Move the supernatant to respective beads for immunoprecipitation using an anti-FLAG antibody (or antibody against the tag).
Allow tubes to rotate at 4°C overnight (12–16 h).
Wash beads 4 times with lysis buffer using conditions described in step 12.
Wash beads 3 more times with TBS using conditions described in step 12.
Remove supernatant, leaving only the beads.
Add 100 μL of TBS for every two dishes of cells to the beads.
For elution using a FLAG-tagged deacetylase, add 3 μL of 3× FLAG Peptide stock (5 mg/mL) for every 100 μL TBS.
Manually agitate the beads by gentle tapping every 5 min for 30 min on ice or rotate at 4°C for 30 min, if sufficient volume is available.
Spin down the beads as described in step 12.
Transfer the supernatant containing the eluted deacetylase into small aliquots for storage at -80°C.
Run a sample of the elutant on an SDS-PAGE gel against a BSA standard curve and stain with Coomassie blue to quantify the concentration of the deacetylase.
Wash the beads bound to the substrate 4 times with lysis buffer.
After washing with lysis buffer, wash the beads 2 times with 1× deacetylation buffer.
Resuspend the beads in 1 ml of deacetylation buffer and equally split the beads into N tubes.
Prepare four reactions below to demonstrate deacetylation of the substrate of interest.
Spin down the beads as described in step 12.
Aspirate all liquid from the tubes using a vacuum or pipette carefully.
Ensure even distribution of the beads in each tube before setting up reactions.
Set up reaction 1 with no deacetylase to show baseline substrate acetylation levels.
Set up reaction 2 by adding only the deacetylase; this should not change acetylation due to lack of NAD+.
Add 50 mM NAD+ stock solution to reaction 3 along with the deacetylase to observe changes in substrate acetylation if deacetylase targets the substrate directly.
Set up reaction 4 by adding deacetylase, 50 mM NAD+, and a deacetylase inhibitor to observe effects on substrate acetylation.
If using a deacetylase-dead mutant instead of wild-type deacetylase, omit nicotinamide and add 0.3 μL dH2O.
For reaction controls, add 4.8 μL NAD+ and 5.1 μL dH2O to check for contamination with class III deacetylases.
Use a 2 M nicotinamide stock to inhibit class III deacetylases.
Incubate the reactions in a 30°C water bath with gentle tapping every 15 min for 3 h.
Add approximately 8 μL of 4× sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) loading buffer after incubation to stop the reaction.
Boil the samples for 5 minutes at 100°C and run on a western blot for analysis, or store at -20°C for later analysis.
